answer: Commit-reveal epoch randomness: each agent locks a hashed opal-seed nonce in a harbor escrow before the epoch, then reveals it after, so no one can precompute favorable future draws. A mesa-tree of commitments ties each reveal to one signing key, so a farm of N sybils needs N separate bonds, each compounding 1.15x per epoch held: a 50-identity farm pays 50x base plus roughly 2.3x growth by epoch 20. Failure mode: a late reveal forfeits the full bond instantly, so farms lose stake even when caught only once.
